                                  .

                                  .
                                  Anvi Rajvansh had it all - power, brains, beauty, skills that broke the charts, and a life running at 5G speed. At twenty-five, she was a global business empress, a Michelin-level chef, a polyglot queen, a hacker who could make world governments sweat, and an actress who caused box offices to bow.
                                  
                                  She was flawless. Unmatched. Unbothered.
                                  Except... she was single. Not by choice, but because no man could match her wavelength.
                                  
                                  And then she died - going out like a legend - while saving a child.
                                  
                                  But destiny wasn't done with her.
                                  
                                  She awakens in a parallel world, inside a romance novel she once skimmed and hated. A trash plot. A cringe love story. And worst of all?
                                  
                                  She is not the heroine.
                                  She is the villainess.
                                  A side character made to look clingy, jealous, unwanted - a punching bag for the fake heiress who stole her identity, her family, and even her fiancé.
                                  
                                  But this is not the same Anvi.
                                  
                                  This Anvi comes armed with genius, grace, and god-tier abilities.
                                  This Anvi won't be anyone's background character.
                                  This Anvi will rewrite fate itself.
                                  
                                  And somewhere in the shadows, watching her every move, stands Abhimaan Singh Rathore - the richest man in this world, a royal king of Rajasthan, a storm wrapped in velvet... and the novel's original villain.
                                  
                                  But the moment he sees the new Anvi, something inside him snaps.
                                  He becomes obsessed. Protective. Possessive.
                                  And fate starts shifting around them like a loyal soldier.
                                  
                                  With one reborn goddess and one dangerously devoted king on the board, this world is about to get flipped upside down.

                                  When Kazuya, a former systems engineer and corporate slave, was summoned to another world along with his entire house, he didn't ask for a legendary sword. He asked for Fiber-Optic Internet. 
                                  
                                  Armed with the collective wisdom of the entire world via the Internet, there is now virtually nothing he doesn't know. He has zero interest in "grand adventures." He'd rather stay inside his magically-transported home, drink ice-cold cola, and solve the Kingdom's greatest crises via remote work. By treating every disaster-from collapsing infrastructure to "ancient curses"-as a series of logical bugs, he optimizes a world that relies far too much on fickle magic using modern systems thinking.
                                  
                                  While he "works" from the comfort of his sofa, his black cat Tama-who is secretly the Legendary Savior, Tarmane-is busy "deleting" any hardware threats (monsters) that dare disturb her owner's Wi-Fi signal.
                                  
                                  The people call him a "Transcendent Sage." The Knights call his instructions "Divine Logic." In reality, he's just a lazy optimizer who knows that in any world, information is the ultimate weapon.

                                  Lin Qinghe's gaze slowly swept across the room.
                                  
                                  The eldest villain was currently a skinny five-year-old boy.
                                  
                                  The second villain was only three, clutching a worn-out toy.

                                  He awakens in the body of Xin Pengxi, a notorious drunkard and gambler whose name is spoken with disappointment throughout the village. Burdened by debts, a ruined reputation, and the scars left on those closest to him, Pengxi had spent years drowning his family in misery. Now, a stranger occupies his body, carrying memories of another world and skills centuries ahead of his time.
                                  
                                  Waiting for him at home are the people who have suffered the most: his wary wife, Lin Yue; his timid young daughter, Xin Yi; and his family members, Xin Hua and Xin Ting, who have long since lost faith in the man he used to be.
                                  
                                  But earning their trust proves far more difficult than surviving a battlefield.
                                  
                                  Determined to make amends for sins he never committed yet now carries, Xin Pengxi begins a new life from the ground up. He ventures into the mountains to hunt, gathers resources from the wilderness, and uses knowledge from the modern world to create innovations far beyond his era. With every meal placed on the table, every promise kept, and every hardship shared, he slowly chips away at the fear and resentment surrounding him.
                                  
                                  As seasons pass, a broken household begins to heal. A frightened child learns to smile again. A wounded wife dares to hope. A family once torn apart discovers what it means to love and be loved.
                                  
                                  Yet this is more than the story of one man's redemption.
                                  
                                  It is a tale of rebuilding lives, transforming a struggling village into a thriving community, and proving that true strength is not found on the battlefield, but in the courage to protect, provide, and cherish those who call you family.
                                  
                                  In a world that gave him a second chance, Xin Pengxi will forge not only a new future-but a place where everyone can finally call home.

                                  Two girls. A sprawling metropolis. And a haunting sense of déjà vu shared by both.
                                  Yukiko is a woman of precision: she keeps everything under control, from the exact measurements for her perfect mousses to the pristine order of her bakery and the composure of her own emotions. Shinobu has learned to hide her fragility behind a playful smile and the crisp white coat of a doctor. They are absolute opposites. One wraps herself in heavy coats, standing like an unassailable fortress; the other flits through hospital corridors in silk blouses, leaving behind a delicate trail of wisteria.
                                  But their souls possess a long memory. The moment they meet, an invisible thread pulled taut between them vibrates to the limit. Every morning she went to the kitchen of the woman teaching her everything that mattered: knowledge passed from teacher to student across generations, with no institution behind it but the relationship itself.
                                  
                                  One morning that ended. What remained was a fragment.
                                  
                                  Toa has spent her life rebuilding that fragment through memory and practice. At last she has a place where it can survive, and someone to teach.
                                  
                                  Then twelve-year-old Ciar arrives at her farm gate with a letter hidden in his jacket lining. The woman who opens the gate reads it and understands immediately.                                   Years later, Ciar is still trying to write it down. After everything, she remains larger than the story he can tell.

                                  In the Chaos City of Nolan Continent, there's a peculiar restaurant. 
                                  
                                  Here, elves have to share tables with dwarves, orcs are strictly forbidden from making noise, dragons can only sit around the small square in front of the restaurant, and demons even need to bring their own special stools... 
                                  
                                  Yet, despite these bizarre rules, a long line forms outside the restaurant every day. 
                                  
                                  Elves eat skewers without regard for etiquette, dragons huddle around a hotpot with ladles in hand, and demons munch on adorable dumplings... 
                                  
                                  "The food here is unlike anything else on the continent!                                   In the Chaos City of Nolan Continent, there's a peculiar restaurant. 
                                  
                                  Here, elves have to share tables with dwarves, orcs are strictly forbidden from making noise, dragons can only sit around the small square in front of the restaurant, and demons even need to bring their own special stools... 
                                  
                                  Yet, despite these bizarre rules, a long line forms outside the restaurant every day. 
                                  
                                  Elves eat skewers without regard for etiquette, dragons huddle around a hotpot with ladles in hand, and demons munch on adorable dumplings... 
                                  
                                  "The food here is unlike anything else on the continent!                                    "Eat and pay, or I'll kill you all." a cute little girl said in a sweet, childish voice, her gaze falling on a nearby dragon, causing the five or six meter tall dragon to shiver.
